pages.title: Otter.ai Public API – Help Center
pages.text:
Otter.ai Public API – Help Center Skip to main content | Help Center Submit a request Submit a request Help Center Otter Enterprise Enterprise Integrations Articles in this section HIPAA | Otter.ai Otter HubSpot for Enterprise Otter Salesforce for Enterprise Add videos to your conversation Connect Jira to Otter.ai CRM Integration: Sync Insights to Custom Fields Directory Sync | SCIM Export to Google Drive Export to Microsoft OneDrive Export to Microsoft SharePoint See more Otter.ai Public API Otter Help October 29, 2026 20:46 Updated Otter.ai’s Public API provides programmatic access to retrieve channels, conversations, transcripts, audio, action items, insights, outlines, and workspace details from your Otter account. Getting Started: Otter's Public API is available for all Enterprise workspaces. If you do not see this feature for your workspace, contact your Otter account manager. API Fundamentals Essential information for authenticating, paging through results, and understanding usage limits. Authentication Create and manage your API keys All API requests require authentication using Bearer token authentication. Follow the steps below to create your API key. Go to Integrations → Developer . Click Create key. Click Copy and store the API key in a safe place. Note: This is only visible once. Make sure you copy the API key in this pop-up. If you forget to copy, follow steps 1-3 to create another key. The API key can now be used. Follow steps 1-4 to create another API key. Note : There is a limit of 2 API keys per user. Using your API key: Include your API key in the Authorization header for every request: Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY ✅ Security best practices: Never share your API key publicly or commit it to version control Store API keys securely using environment variables or secrets management Rotate API keys periodically Rate Limits Enterprise plan users are currently limited to 10 requests / second. If you exceed your rate limit, you'll receive a 429 Too Many Requests response. Pagination List endpoints use cursor-based pagination for efficient data retrieval. Pagination Response { "meta": { "retrieved_at": "2025-07-31T12:00:00Z", "has_more": true, "next_cursor": "next_cursor_position" }, "data": [ /* array of results */ ] } Meta Fields: Field Type Description retrieved_at string Timestamp when data was retrieved (ISO 8601 format) has_more boolean Whether more pages are available next_cursor string (optional) Cursor for the next page Usage To retrieve the next page, use the next_cursor value in your next request's cursor query parameter: GET /conversations?cursor=next_cursor_position&limit=20 Continue paginating until has_more is false . Webhooks Webhooks are the recommended way to build export integrations with Otter. Instead of constantly polling the API to check for new conversations or action items, webhooks push real-time notifications to your application the moment events occur. This makes webhooks ideal for automatically syncing meeting summaries to your CRM, sending action items to project management tools, or triggering custom workflows whenever a transcript is ready. By using webhooks, you'll build more efficient integrations that respond instantly to changes while staying well within API rate limits. Learn more: Learn how to set up webhooks with our workspace webhook documentation . Endpoints Explore the available API endpoints, grouped by type. Channel Endpoints for retrieving channel data A Channel lets you organize Conversations. GET /channels GET /channels/{id}/members GET /channels Use this endpoint to list channels for the authenticated user. Results are returned in alphabetical order by channel name. Example Request: curl -X GET "https://api.otter.ai/v1/channels" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" Response: Returns a ChannelListResponse with channel data. meta : Response metadata, including retrieved_at data : An array of channel objects { "meta": { "retrieved_at": "2025-07-31T12:00:00Z" }, "data": [ { "id": "channel_id", "name": "backend product meeting", "member_count": 50, "owner": { "id": "user_id", "name": "Jane Doe", "first_name": "Jane", "last_name": "Doe", "email": "Jane@test.com" }, "discoverability": "private" } ] } Channel object: Field Type Description id string Unique channel identifier name string Name of the channel member_count integer Number of members in the channel owner User Owner of the channel discoverability string Channel visibility setting, such as private or workspace (public) Error Response(s): Status Description 400 Invalid request parameters GET /channels/{id}/members Use this endpoint to list all members in a specific channel. Results are returned in alphabetical order by member name. Path Parameter: Parameter Type Required Description id string Yes Channel ID Example Request: curl -X GET "https://api.otter.ai/v1/channels/{id}/members" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" Response: Returns a ChannelMembersResponse containing a list of users in the channel. meta: Response metadata, including retrieved_at data: An array of user objects { "meta": { "retrieved_at": "2026-04-23T18:57:09Z" }, "data": [ { "id": "a1B2c3D4e5F6g7H8", "name": "Jane Doe", "first_name": "Jane", "last_name": "Doe", "email": "jane.doe@example.com" }, { "id": "h8G7f6E5d4C3b2A1", "name": "John Smith", "first_name": "John", "last_name": "Smith", "email": "john.smith@example.com" }, { "id": "z9Y8x7W6v5U4t3S2", "name": "Alex Johnson", "first_name": "Alex", "last_name": "Johnson", "email": "alex.johnson@example.com" } ] } User Object: Field Type Description id string Unique user identifier name string Full name of the user first_name string User’s first name last_name string User’s last name email string User’s email address Error Responses: Status Description 400 Invalid request parameters 404 Channel not found Conversations Endpoints to create, list, and retrieve conversations, including conversation details and audio downloads POST /conversations GET /conversations GET /conversations/{id} GET /conversations/{id}/audio POST /conversations Creates a new conversation from a file. This is useful if you are importing calls into Otter, such as from a Dialer. Request Body: Field Type Required Description file string (URL) Yes URL to the file to process name string No Name for the conversation Example Request: curl -X POST "https://api.otter.ai/v1/conversations" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "file": "https://example.com/file.mp4", "name": "Product Launch Meeting" }' Response: Returns a ConversationCreateResponse with status. { "status": "success", "completed_at": "2025-12-01 01:00:00Z", "file": "audio.mp3" } GET /conversations Use this endpoint to list conversations for the authenticated user. Results are returned in reverse chronological order (most recent first) and use cursor-based pagination for efficient retrieval. You can optionally include shared conversations or filter results by channel. Tip : Use workspace webhooks to receive Conversation data in real-time! Query Parameters: Parameter Type Required Description include_shared boolean No Whether to include conversations shared with the user. Default: false. Automatically set to true if channel_id is provided channel_id string No Filter conversations by channel ID. Overrides include_shared limit integer No Number of items to return per page. Minimum: 1, Maximum: 20 cursor string No Cursor for pagination. Use the next_cursor value from the previous response to retrieve the next page Example Request: curl -X GET "https://api.otter.ai/v1/conversations?include_shared=false&channel_id=&limit=20&cursor=" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" Response: Returns a ConversationListResponse with conversation data and pagination metadata. meta : Pagination metadata, including retrieved_at, has_more, and next_cursor data : An array of conversation objects { "meta": { "retrieved_at": "2025-07-31T12:00:00Z", "has_more": true, "next_cursor": "next_cursor_position" }, "data": [ { "id": "conversation_id", "title": "product launch meeting", "url": "https://otter.ai/u/conversation_id", "owner": { "id": "user_id", "name": "Jane Doe", "first_name": "Jane", "last_name": "Doe", "email": "Jane@test.com" }, "created_at": "2025-07-31T12:00:00Z", "process_status": { "abstract_summary": null, "action_item": null, "outline": null }, "calendar_guests": [ { "name": "John Doe", "email": "john@test.com" } ], "shared_emails": [ { "email": "hello@example.com", "user": { "id": "user_id", "name": "Jane Doe", "first_name": "Jane", "last_name": "Doe", "email": "Jane@test.com" }, "permission": "collaborate" } ], "shared_channels": [ { "channel": { "id": "channel_id", "name": "backend product meeting", "member_count": 50, "owner": { "id": "user_id", "name": "Jane Doe", "first_name": "Jane", "last_name": "Doe", "email": "Jane@test.com" }, "discoverability": "private" }, "permission": "collaborate" } ], "abstract_summary": "This meeting discussed the next steps in the project launch", "conf_join_url": "https://zoom.us/j/1234567890" } ] } Pagination: has_more : Indicates whether additional results are available next_cursor : Use this value in the next request to retrieve the next page Conversation created_at string Timestamp when the conversation was created process_status object Processing status for generated data such as summary, action items, and outline calendar_guests array List of calendar guests associated with the conversation shared_emails array List of users or email addresses the conversation is shared with shared_channels array List of channels the conversation is shared with abstract_summary string Generated summary of the conversation conf_join_url string Conferencing join URL associated with the conversation Shared channel object: Field Type Description id string Unique channel identifier name string Name of the channel member_count integer Number of members in the channel owner User Owner of the channel discoverability string Channel visibility setting, such as private or workspace (public) Error Responses: Status Description 400 Invalid filter or pagination parameters 404 Channel not found GET /conversations/{id} Use this endpoint to get the summary and details of a specific conversation. You can optionally include additional conversation data such as action items, insights, outlines, transcript, or all available relationships. Tip : Use workspace webhooks to receive Conversation data in real-time! Path Parameters: Parameter Type Required Description id string Yes Conversation ID Query Parameters: Parameter Type Required Description include string Yes Comma-separated list of additional data to include. Options: action_items , insights , outline , transcript , all . If all is specified, all available relationship fields are returned. Example: insights,transcript Example Request: curl -X GET "https://api.otter.ai/v1/conversations/{id}?include=action_items" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" Response: Returns a ConversationResponse with conversation details and requested relationships. meta : Response metadata, including retrieved_at data : The conversation object relationships : Additional related data returned when requested with the include parameter { "meta": { "retrieved_at": "2025-07-31T12:00:00Z" }, "data": { "relationships": { "action_items": [ { "id": "action_item_id", "text": "Follow up with the sales team", "assignee": { "id": "user_id", "name": "Jane Doe", "first_name": "Jane", "last_name": "Doe", "email": "Jane@test.com" }, "status": { "completed": true, "created_at": "2025-07-31T12:00:00Z", "last_modified_at": "2025-07-31T12:00:00Z", "completed_at": "2025-07-31T12:00:00Z" } } ], "insights": null, "outline": null, "transcript": null, "custom_prompt": null }, "id": Path Parameters: Parameter Type Required Description id string Yes Conversation ID Example Request: curl -X GET "https://api.otter.ai/v1/conversations/{id}/audio" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" Response: Returns an AudioResponse containing the MP3 audio download link. meta : Response metadata, including retrieved_at data : The audio object { "meta": { "retrieved_at": "2025-07-31T12:00:00Z" }, "data": { "url": "https://test.com/audio.mp3" } } Audio Object: Field Type Description url string Download URL for the MP3 audio file Error Response: Status Description 404 Conversation not found Workspace Endpoints to access workspace details, member usage, and workspace analytics GET /workspace GET /workspace/{id}/analytics GET /workspace Use this endpoint to get the workspace for the authenticated user. The response includes workspace details such as the workspace ID, name, owner, member count, handle, and type. Example Request: curl -X GET "https://api.otter.ai/v1/workspace" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" Response: Returns a WorkspaceGetResponse containing the authenticated user’s workspace details. meta : Response metadata, including retrieved_at data : The authenticated user’s workspace object { "meta": { "retrieved_at": "2025-07-31T12:00:00Z" }, "data": { "id": 42, "name": "workspace name", "owner": { "id": "user_id", "name": "Jane Doe", "first_name": "Jane", "last_name": "Doe", "email": "Jane@test.com" }, "member_count": 50, "handle": "otter.ai", "type": "business" } } Workspace object: Field Type Description id integer Unique workspace identifier name string Name of the workspace owner User Owner of the workspace member_count integer Number of members in the workspace handle string Workspace handle (e.g., domain or identifier like otter.ai) type string Type of workspace (e.g., business) Error responses: Status Description 404 User not in a workspace GET /workspace/{id}/analytics Use this endpoint to retrieve workspace usage analytics for a date range, including total transcribed minutes, conversation counts, current license counts, and per-member usage sorted by name. Operation ID: getWorkspaceAnalytics Base URL: https://api.otter.ai/v1 Path Parameters: Parameter Type Required Description id string Yes Workspace ID. Use GET /workspace to retrieve your workspace details, including its ID. Query Parameters: Parameter Type Required Description start_date string (date) No Inclusive start date in yyyy-mm-dd format. Omit together with end_date to use the last 30 days. If only start_date is provided, the end of the range defaults to now. end_date string (date) No Inclusive end date in yyyy-mm-dd format. Cannot be provided without start_date . timezone string No IANA timezone used to interpret dates, such as America/Los_Angeles . Defaults to the workspace timezone, then America/Los_Angeles . Date range behavior: Omit both dates to retrieve analytics for the last 30 days. Provide only start_date to use now as the end of the range. Providing only end_date is invalid. When both dates are provided, the range is inclusive, from 00:00:00 on the start date through 23:59:59 on the end date in the resolved timezone. Note: num_of_minutes , num_of_conversations , and members are scoped to the resolved report window. seats_used and seats_invoiced are current license counts and are not historical values for the report window. Example Request: curl -X GET "https://api.otter.ai/v1/workspace/{id}/analytics?start_date=2026-09-01&end_date=2026-09-30&timezone=America%2FLos_Angeles" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" Replace {id} with your workspace ID. This GET request has no request body. Response: A successful request returns 200 OK with content type application/json and a WorkspaceAnalyticsResponse . meta : Response metadata, including retrieved_at data : The workspace analytics object for the resolved date range The following example uses illustrative values. { "meta": { "retrieved_at": "2026-10-01T12:00:00Z" }, "data": { "start_date": "2026-09-01", "end_date": "2026-09-30", "timezone": "America/Los_Angeles", "num_of_minutes": 120, "num_of_conversations": 4, "seats_used": 1, "seats_invoiced": 5, "members": [ { "id": "hashed_user_id", "name": "Jane Doe", "email": "jane@example.com", "status": "Activated", "num_of_conversations": 4, "num_of_minutes": 120, "average_conversations_per_month": 4, "average_minutes_per_conversation": 30, "average_minutes_per_month": 120, "join_date": "2026-08-15", "last_activity_at": "2026-09-30T18:30:00Z", "last_login_at": "2026-09-30T16:00:00Z", "num_of_ai_chats": 2, "num_of_conversations_shared_by_user": 2, "num_of_conversations_shared_with_user": 0, "num_of_conversations_viewed": 4 } ] } } Response fields: Field Type Required Description meta object (CommonMeta) Yes Response metadata. meta.retrieved_at string (date-time) Yes Timestamp when the data was retrieved (ISO 8601 format). data object (WorkspaceAnalytics) Yes Workspace analytics for the resolved report window. Workspace analytics object: Field Type Required Description start_date string (date) Yes Resolved inclusive start date of the report window ( yyyy-mm-dd ). end_date string (date) Yes Resolved inclusive end date of the report window ( yyyy-mm-dd ). timezone string Yes IANA timezone used to interpret dates. Defaults to the workspace timezone, then America/Los_Angeles . num_of_minutes number Yes Total transcribed minutes for workspace members in the report window. num_of_conversations number Yes Total conversations created by workspace members in the report window. seats_used integer Yes Current licensed seats in use. Not scoped to the report window. seats_invoiced integer Yes Current invoiced seat quantity. Not scoped to the report window. members array of WorkspaceAnalyticsMember objects Yes Per-member usage for the report window, sorted by name. Workspace analytics member object: Field Type Required Description id string Yes Opaque hashed user ID. name string Yes Member name. email string (email) Yes Member email address. status string Yes Member status: Activated , Deactivated , or Pending . num_of_conversations number Yes Conversations created by this member in the report window. num_of_minutes number Yes Minutes transcribed by this member in the report window. average_conversations_per_month number Yes Average number of conversations per month. average_minutes_per_conversation number Yes Average transcribed minutes per conversation. average_minutes_per_month number Yes Average transcribed minutes per month. join_date string (date) or null No Member join date in the report timezone, or null if unknown. last_activity_at string (date-time) or null No Most recent conversation creation, conversation view, or annotation timestamp, or null if none. last_login_at string (date-time) or null No Most recent login timestamp, or null if the member has never logged in. num_of_ai_chats number or null No AI chats created by this member in the report window, or null if unavailable. num_of_conversations_shared_by_user number or null No Conversations shared by this member in the report window, or null if unavailable. num_of_conversations_shared_with_user number or null No Conversations shared with this member in the report window, or null if unavailable. num_of_conversations_viewed number or null No Conversations viewed by this member in the report window, or null if unavailable. Error responses: Status Description 400 Bad Request Invalid date range, timezone, or workspace ID. This includes providing end_date without start_date . 403 Forbidden Caller is not a workspace admin. 404 Not Found Workspace not found. Errors use content type application/json and an ErrorResponse object containing a required errors array. The response schemas are ValidationErrorResponse (400), ForbiddenErrorResponse (403), and NotFoundErrorResponse (404). Error response fields: Field Type Required Description errors array of RequestError objects Yes Details about the request errors. errors[].status string No HTTP error status text. errors[].code string No Specific error code defined by Otter. errors[].detail string No Description of the error. errors[].source object (RequestErrorSource) No Information about the request source. May be null , as shown in the example below. errors[].source.header string No Header information associated with the error. errors[].source.parameter string No Request parameter information associated with the error. errors[].source.pointer string (URI) No URI identifying the request source associated with the error. Example Error Response (403): { "errors": [ { "status": "Forbidden", "code": "403", "detail": "User has no permission", "source": null } ] } 👉 Best Practices Rate Limiting Implement appropriate rate limiting in your application to avoid overwhelming the API. Consider implementing exponential backoff for retries. Error Handling Always check for and handle error responses gracefully. Parse the error details to provide meaningful feedback to users. Pagination Use cursor-based pagination for large result sets. Don't attempt to retrieve all data in a single request. Selective Loading Use the include parameter in conversation endpoints to fetch only the data you need. This reduces response payload size and improves performance. Caching Cache responses where appropriate to reduce API calls. Consider implementing a caching layer for frequently accessed data. Field Selection When using the include parameter, only request the fields you actually need rather than using all Related to api Was this article helpful? pages.text: Otter MCP Server – Help Center Skip to main content | Help Center Submit a request Submit a request Help Center Using Otter Otter AI Chat Articles in this section Otter AI Chat Overview Asking Otter AI Chat questions Generate content with Otter AI Chat Image Enriched Conversation AI Chat Opt out of Otter AI Chat Otter AI Chat FAQs Otter AI Chat is not showing Otter AI Chat: Add Context (Channels, Conversations, or Folders) Otter MCP Server Troubleshooting Otter AI Chat See more Otter MCP Server Otter Help October 30, 2026 21:11 Updated Connect AI models to Otter using Model Context Protocol (MCP). Connecting Otter MCP to your AI applications enables secure, scalable access to various language model understandings to power features like smarter summaries, contextual suggestions, and automated insights for all your Otter conversations and meetings. Learn to connect to Claude , ChatGPT , Cursor , Perplexity , or other platforms . What is Model Context Protocol (MCP)? MCP is an open standard that allows AI assistants like Claude and ChatGPT to securely access external data sources. With Otter’s MCP Server, these AI assistants can: ✅ Search your meeting transcripts across all time periods ✅ Analyze patterns and themes across multiple meetings ✅ Generate content using your actual meeting data ✅ Surface insights without leaving your AI workflow 🔑 Key advantage: Your meeting knowledge becomes instantly accessible to AI assistants, eliminating manual copy-paste and context-switching. 🔒 Security: All access is OAuth-authenticated with granular permissions. Your AI assistant can only access meetings you explicitly authorize. Claude setup Learn how to set up Claude Check out Otter.ai in the Claude connectors directory . Connect Otter MCP to Claude. Go to Settings → Connectors → Browse connectors. Note: If your workspace admin has already added Otter.ai, it will appear as an available connector. Click Connect and proceed directly to Step 3. Go to Claude's Otter.ai page and click Connect. Sign in to your Otter account. Review the info and click Authorize access to connect with Claude. Otter MCP is connected to Claude. Enable Otter MCP tool with chat Click on the search and tools menu in the chat box. Toggle on Otter. Configure your Otter MCP tool permissions Claude will prompt for permissions when querying using Otter MCP tools. You can manage permissions for the Otter MCP tool in the connector settings. Under the settings Connectors, click Configure next to Otter or manage through the 3-dot menu. Manage each of the tools' permissions. We recommend setting it to Always allow . ChatGPT setup Learn how to set up ChatGPT Connect Otter MCP to ChatGPT. Otter.ai is available in the ChatGPT App Store. Check out Otter.ai in the ChatGPT App Store . Sign in to the ChatGPT web version. Go to Settings . Note: To connect to Otter MCP, you must currently complete the connection through the web version of Otter . Connecting directly through the desktop app is not yet supported. Once the connection is established on the web, it will automatically be available in the desktop app. Go to Apps and add apps. The option may vary depending on your existing account. Go to Otter.ai in the ChatGPT App Store . Click Connect. Carefully review the information and click Connect Otter.ai . Sign in to your Otter.ai account. Carefully review the information and click Authorize access to proceed. Otter.ai is now connected to your ChatGPT account. Enable Otter MCP tools with ChatGPT. Now that Otter is connected, you can work from the ChatGPT web browser or the desktop app. Click the + (plus icon). Click ••• More and select Otter.ai . Type @ and select Otter.ai . When starting a new chat, make sure Otter.ai is showing. If you do not see otter.ai, select it again through the steps above. Using Otter MCP tools with ChatGPT Otter uses 3 tools in ChatGPT to query your meetings: fetch get user info search If prompted, accept the tool request to proceed. You can click any source to go directly to the Otter conversation. If you are experiencing any issues querying your Otter conversations, we recommend specifically mentioning the Otter tool you want to use in your query. Manage Otter MCP settings for ChatGPT in Apps. Cursor setup Learn how to set up Cursor Connect Otter MCP to Cursor. Refer to Cursor’s documentation on connecting MCP servers for more info . Navigate to Cursor settings. Click Tools & MCP. Click Add Custom MCP. Configure the JSON file with the following. Save changes to the file . { "mcpServers": { "otter_meeting_mcp": { "url": "https://mcp.otter.ai/mcp" } } } Navigate back to Tools & MCP. Click Connect . Click Open . Sign in to your Otter account. Click Authorize access. Otter MCP is connected to Cursor. Enable Cursor Enable Otter MCP by ensuring it's toggled ON under Cursor Tools & MCP settings and tools enabled. Cursor will automatically use available tools. If a tool is disabled, click on the grayed-out tool to re-enable. Perplexity Learn how to set up Perplexity Connect Otter MCP to Perplexity using custom connectors to securely access and reference your Otter conversations, meeting notes, and AI insights directly within Perplexity. Note: Perplexity’s UI may change over time. Refer to Perplexity’s documentation for the latest instructions on connecting a custom connector. Navigate to the Connectors settings page. The location may vary depending on whether you are using an individual or an Enterprise account. Click + Custom connector. Configure using the following settings and click Add. Name: Otter.ai Description: Meetings from Otter MCP server URL: https://mcp.otter.ai/mcp Icon: The Otter icon can be downloaded here. Sign in to your Otter account and click Authorize access. Otter MCP is connected to Perplexity. Enable Perplexity Make sure the connector is enabled before submitting your query. You may need to grant permissions the first time you use the provided tools . Connect Otter MCP to other AI tools You may be able to connect Otter MCP to your AI tool depending on your platform Otter MCP can be connected to third-party AI tools that support the Model Context Protocol (MCP) using a JSON configuration file. Setup varies by platform and is managed entirely within your AI tool’s configuration. Configuration, behavior, and support depend on the specific platform you are using. Refer to your tool's documentation to connect to an MCP server. Before you begin Your AI tool must support MCP You should be familiar with editing JSON configuration files OAuth authentication is still required to connect JSON Configuration file { "mcpServers": { "otter": { "url": "https://mcp.otter.ai/mcp" } } } Complete setup in your AI tool Add a custom MCP and configure the JSON file with the above. Connect and authenticate with your Otter account. Verify the Otter MCP server appears, and tools are available. Note: We’ll continue adding step-by-step guides for more AI tools. In the meantime, setup may vary by platform and is completed at your discretion. Tools overview Name Description Sample prompt Get user info Get the current user's name and email. This tool retrieves the authenticated user's profile information, including their name and email address. “What is my email address?” Search Search for meetings and get an overview of information. "Which meetings related to product improvement did I attend in Q2?" Fetch Retrieves a full speech transcript of a meeting or conversation. "What are the three main focus areas based on marketing meetings with our Enterprise clients?" “ Summarize the presentation https://otter.ai/u/NpsJNrxvrcDay0dnlPKPZM87OSo?tab=chat&view=summary” Fetch example Query direct conversation URLs. Copy an Otter conversation URL from the browser. Note: The conversation must be shared with you for your AI application to access the content. Try it out by replacing the following with your own conversation link: Summarize the presentation https://otter.ai/u/NpsJNrxvrcDay0dnlPKPZM87OSo?tab=chat&view=summary Examples & usage Query conversations, pull highlights and key details, and generate content based on your meetings. Examples Generate a PowerPoint based on meeting XYZ. In which meetings did we discuss mobile navigation UX? Pull all meetings in Q3 discussing sales initiatives and the top ideas. Advanced Use Cases Competitive Intelligence Analysis “Analyze all Q4 customer calls mentioning competitors. What are the top 3 feature requests we’re losing deals over?” Onboarding Acceleration “Pull highlights from all sales training meetings in the last month. Create a structured onboarding doc with key processes and best practices.” Executive Briefings “Summarize the key decisions and action items from all leadership meetings this week. Format as a Friday exec briefing.” Cross-Functional Alignment “Compare what Product and Sales are saying about our Q1 roadmap. Identify any misalignments or gaps in messaging.” Historical Context Retrieval “What did we decide about the pricing model in our August strategy meeting? Pull the exact discussion and reasoning.” Meeting Prep Intelligence “I have a call with Acme Corp tomorrow. Pull all previous meetings with them and summarize: current status, open issues, and key stakeholders.” FAQs Is Otter MCP available for all AI applications? We are working to release Otter MCP for all AI applications. Contact our Otter Support Team for help setting up Otter MCP with your AI application. Note: Google Gemini's support for MCP tools is not yet available, according to this thread ; however, Gemini's command line interface (CLI) does support connecting to MCPs . Refer to Google's documentation for the most up-to-date information. Is Google Gemini supported? No. According to this thread , Google Gemini does not yet support MCP tools. However, Gemini's command line interface (CLI) does support connecting to MCPs . Note: Refer to Google's documentation for the most up-to-date information. What meetings can I access through the MCP Server? You can access all meetings that you have captured in Otter, as well as any meetings shared with you from other users in your Workspace. Learn more about conversation sharing and Channels in Otter. Can I connect Otter MCP on the ChatGPT desktop app? Connecting Otter MCP on ChatGPT desktop app is not yet available. Connect Otter MCP on the web version of ChatGPT . Is there a public API key for me to set up Otter MCP for my AI application? We currently do not have a public API key at this time. Contact our Otter Support team for help setting up Otter MCP with your AI application. Where can I download the Otter icon? You download the Otter.ai icon at the end of this article.
